sections.start_here_text: The CAT I rules that moved: drifted from the checklist, or failing since they passed. CAT II and III are in the tables below.
sections.text: These rules passed on the host in an earlier scan and fail now, and the checklist has them as Not a Finding: the host moved away from its checklist. Fix the host, or - if the change was approved - update the review in STIG Manager (this job never writes to it). They stay here every run until one of the two is done. CAT I is critical, CAT II and III a warning (check_stig_severity).
sections.title: 1. Drifted - the host fails what STIG Manager has as Not a Finding

rows: RHEL 9 must automatically exit interactive command shell user sessions after 10 minutes of inactivity.

sections.text: Something changed on the host since these passed (the scans are kept on the host, check_stig_dir). STIG Manager has no Not a Finding for them, so they are not drift from the checklist - but they are new. Once the review is Open, they leave this table.
sections.title: 2. New fails - passed in an earlier scan

sections.text: The checklist has these as Not a Finding, and they have failed in every scan of the host: nothing moved that this job saw. Either the host was like this before its first scan, or the scanner checks the rule another way than DISA's check text (OpenSCAP's check, or what Evaluate-STIG found, is the last column; the scan's report on the host shows more). For each: fix the host, set the review to Open, or - the scanner is wrong for your site - add the rule to check_stig_ignore_rules. Report only (check_stig_disagree_severity: warning makes them findings).

sections.text: Pass and Fail count STIG rules (several SCAP checks of one rule count once, one SCAP check of several rules counts for each); the rest are not applicable or not checked automatically. Left out: fails of the rules in check_stig_ignore_rules. Each scan's report (OpenSCAP), results or checklist (Evaluate-STIG) and summary stay on the host.
